problem: Image-goal navigation systems depend on temporally ordered video or auxiliary sensors (depth, LiDAR, odometry); with only unordered RGB image collections they suffer perceptual aliasing, spurious topological edges, oscillating actions and error accumulation.
motivation: Crowd-sourced or pre-recorded image sets (e.g. real-estate photos) have no temporal order or odometry, so sequence-based topological navigation cannot be deployed on them. The paper argues that mapping, localization and planning must be co-designed so errors are suppressed at every stage.
key_idea: Build a 2D topological graph from unordered RGB images via one-shot calibrated geometric verification plus maximum spanning forest with loop reinsertion, then localize with an entropy-adaptive graph belief filter and plan/replan widest paths on it.
insight: Retrieval-only graphs trade precision for recall. Table 4 ablation: the top-k ANN baseline gets P 0.1245, the adaptive threshold without MSF gets P 0.6910 but R 0.4220, and the full method gets F1 0.7365, so the MSF fixes the fragmentation left by strict local verification. Localization: disabling entropy-adaptive fusion drops accuracy from 95.49 to 90.57. Navigation: replacing BPL with temporal-distance localization drops SR from 68.1 to 59.6, so VPR-based global belief matters.
method: RAVEL retrieval and calibration: MegaLoc global descriptors indexed in FAISS; two anchor images (a random one and its farthest neighbor) are matched exhaustively with LightGlue, and 2-means clustering of inlier counts gives the inlier threshold tau=(min S_h+max S_l)/2 and the descriptor radius d_VPR.

RAVEL verification and pruning: candidate pairs within d_VPR are verified with LightGlue, and edge weight is the inlier count if it exceeds tau; a Maximum Spanning Forest (Kruskal) gives a compact backbone, then strong loop edges with W>tau_add (1.5*tau) are reinserted.
BPL prediction: multi-hop transition matrix T from row-normalized sum of A^m, m=0..K (K=3), so belief diffuses over graph neighborhoods without odometry.

BPL adaptive fusion: observation likelihood exp(-lambda*||z_t-z_i||^2); the prior and likelihood are fused by a weighted geometric mean with weights set from the normalized entropy of the belief (higher entropy means more weight on observation); the MAP node is the location estimate.

BASS planning: start node from MAP of initial belief and goal node by descriptor similarity; widest path (max-min edge weight, Dijkstra) is computed; subgoal images are passed to a local image-based policy (ViNT / NoMaD).

BASS replanning: deviation is declared if the MAP node leaves the path or lies more than 3 graph hops from the subgoal, triggering a new widest path from the current MAP node; success when goal belief exceeds 0.5.
Benchmark pipeline: Isaac Sim GRScenes scenes (10 scenes, 3,594 images) with ground-truth topology from ESDF medial-axis skeleton and node sampling.

setting.backbone: MegaLoc (VPR descriptor) + LightGlue matcher for mapping/localization (pretrained, not retrained); ViNT or NoMaD as the local planner
setting.training_data: No new training for ULVN itself (pretrained MegaLoc, LightGlue, ViNT, NoMaD); the '-A' ablations retrain the local planners with only the action-head loss
setting.observation: monocular RGB only (unordered image library plus live RGB); no depth, odometry or temporal order
setting.action_space: low-level velocity commands from the image-goal local planner (ViNT/NoMaD)
setting.simulator: NVIDIA Isaac Sim (GRScenes); CARLA for RAVEL/BPL analysis; real-world Diablo robot
setting.privileged: none at test time (ground-truth topology is used only for evaluation)

numbers_note: No standard benchmark (R2R, ObjNav etc.) is used; all results are on the authors' own GRScenes-based unordered-landmark benchmark. The navigation table does not give the number of episodes. The paper's own 'ULVN+ViNT-A' (SR 31.0) and 'ULVN+NoMaD-A' (SR 54.3) are additional variants. The BPL prediction weights in the main text (w_p=1-H) differ from the appendix piecewise-linear definition, and lambda differs (5 vs 10 vs adaptive).
results: ULVN+NoMaD reaches SR 71.9 with 0.42 avg collisions, and ULVN+ViNT reaches SPL 0.8398. Both beat UniGoal (SR 61.6, SPL 0.3176) and Uni-NaVid (SR 32.0). RAVEL gets F1 0.7365 vs 0.6043 for PlaceNav top-2, BPL localization accuracy is 95.49% vs 91.09% for MegaLoc, and the system was demonstrated on a real Diablo robot.
limitations: Navigation SR (~71%) lags localization accuracy (~95%) because the local planners have weak obstacle perception and oscillate.

Evaluation is on a self-built simulated benchmark (10 Isaac Sim scenes) with a single qualitative real-world trial; it needs enough visual overlap in the image library and struggles in texture-poor or large open areas.
Manual hyperparameters (K=3, D_thres=3, loop threshold 1.5*tau) and inconsistent method descriptions between main text and appendix; SPL values are not comparable in scale with the baselines' SPL.
